meta.title: Roadmark expanded Australian BEV road-vehicle market inventory
meta.scope: All new battery-electric road vehicles in Australia: passenger cars, SUVs, people movers, vans, utes, light/medium/heavy trucks and buses. Motorcycles/scooters and non-pedal road trikes with cited road-use evidence and specialist low-volume imports are open census categories. Universe remains unclosed.
notes: This is market-audit evidence, not a complete ranked specification dataset.
Stock labels describe source advertisements only when their configuration and new condition are supported; physical units and allocation remain separate. Demonstrators are not treated as new stock.
Trims are exact named configurations verified in sources, not necessarily all configurations if trimCoverage is partial.
Model year, source publication date and observation date are distinct.
No missing numeric specifications were inferred.
Counts include named equipment/package configurations and some future-delivery entries. They are not counts of all current Australian marketing grades or all immediately available vehicles.
User scope clarified 2026-10-10 to all new EV road-vehicle types. Rank by compatible class/measurement cohort; passenger metrics must not silently rank against buses/trucks.
Motorcycle/scooter offerings with supplier road-use claims are included; per-VIN/state registration and complete universe remain unverified.

Lexus ES350e/500e BEV family newly reconciled on 10 October 2026; this historical reconciliation is retained; the audit at that checkpoint contained 231 model records, including unresolved/future/withdrawn entries, not 231 currently buyable vehicles.

records.evidenceNote: Historical evidence note recorded 2026-10-10, retained verbatim for context: "Current manufacturer product page markets Element; manufacturer news identifies the second-generation Element 2. Kept as one model family." Current-source update observed 2026-10-11: Current manufacturer-linked Australian documents identify Element 2.2 in 12.0 m (12,055 mm; 6,580 mm wheelbase) and 10.9 m (10,900 mm; 5,425 mm wheelbase) length options, with CATL LFP batteries and Driventic VEDS 1.5 HD drive. These are published length options within the existing family; exact layouts/builds, orders and stock remain unverified.
limitations: Generation, battery chemistry and pack-count configurations must be quoted against the current build specification. Do not turn the historical Element and Element 2 names into two independent model families. Open orders and stock unverified.

The 2026-10-11 check is the sealed packet's observation of current manufacturer linkage and source captures, not a recheck of every historical source or the full market. Original evidence history and source dates are retained.

Current Element 2.2 CATL LFP / Driventic VEDS 1.5 HD evidence is separate from earlier Element 2 NMC / ZF CeTrax and original Element LMP / Actia. Earlier 10.5 m, 383/462 kWh and 450 kW pantograph claims must not migrate to 2.2. Current ZF axles or telematics do not identify the drive motor as CeTrax.

The two published length options are 12.0 m (12,055 mm; 6,580 mm wheelbase) and 10.9 m (10,900 mm; 5,425 mm wheelbase). The shared technical table is not proof of separately validated battery, door or layout builds for each length. These options add no trims, generations, detailed configurations or vehicle counts.

411.5 kWh usable energy is explicit in the current brochure and product asset. The specification literally prints 411.5 kW in its energy field on pages 1 and 2; that unit defect is preserved in the sidecar. Gross energy, traction pack count and traction voltage remain unknown; the 24 V lithium declaration is auxiliary only.

For 12.0 m, specification page 2 declares 39 seated / up to 26 standing / up to 65 total, while brochure page 5 declares 43 seated / 26 standing / 69 total. Normalized long-bus seating and total remain null; no metadata-date, wheelchair, door-count or driver arithmetic resolves the conflict.

The 10.9 m sample layout declares 37 seated / up to 23 standing / up to 60 total. Wheelchair-dependent seating declarations and one/two-door advertising remain source-scoped sample or option evidence, not exact purchasable builds. No length × door × wheelchair cross-product is admitted, and driver-count basis remains unresolved.

Specification and brochure PDF creation/modification metadata are 8 and 18 September 2026 respectively, not visible technical issue dates, production dates or formal model years. The specification metadata title names 12 m, while its visible table and sample layouts include both lengths. No selected build or issue/model-year bridge is established.

Up-to-500 km / SORT 1–Urban / ZEMO is a duty-cycle-qualified manufacturer claim, not independently validated range or passenger WLTP. Brochure 0.72 kWh/km and asset 72.01 kWh/100 km remain separate source values. 300 kW maximum DC and CCS2 DC ports do not establish a charge-time/SOC curve, AC or pantograph capability for 2.2.

Battery warranty is a qualified headline with contract applicability unverified: specification page 1 states up to 15 years / 1.5 million km; brochure page 3 supports only up to 15 years. Destination display, CCTV and passenger information are pre-wired; optional equipment remains optional, not delivered standard fitment.

Manufacturer-built complete buses and a current product consultation/download route are evidenced, but no accepted procurement build, New stock unit, VIN, allocation, price, delivery commitment or independently checked Australian road approval is established. Existing order, stock, registration, model-year and ranking holds remain unchanged.

reconciledLeads.resolutionNote: The current Australian BZL chassis range includes Volvo BZL Electric Articulated (BZLA). Volvo and Volgren identify a PTA-specific 18 m Optimus eBus articulated completed build, with 57 source-described seats and 497 kWh total installed energy. PTA confirmed the first delivery in July 2026; current general orders for that exact complete build, specific New stock, model-matched road approval and actual passenger-service entry remain unverified. This is one BZL family with distinct chassis and customer-build evidence, not an additional currently purchasable complete vehicle.

originalRecord.evidenceNote: Official June 2026 news confirms the Australian articulated electric bus unveiling with a local body.
limitations: Could be a BZL configuration rather than another family. Confirm model designation, order opening and approval before expanding the main BZL entry.

retainedCommercialAndApprovalHolds: Identity reconciliation only. Articulated remains within BZL; no independent family, exact trim, detailed variant or ranking addition.

The PTA customer build is 497 kWh total installed, not usable energy. Generic articulated chassis 500/530 kWh options and 250 kW CCS/450 kW OppCharge declarations are separate scopes and must not be substituted.

57 source-described seats has no verified driver-inclusive definition or exact accessible-layout scope. Approximately 105 seated-and-standing passengers is not a seat count; do not subtract to derive standing capacity.
No exact completed-build VTA/RVD/RAV/state-registration proof was retrieved. The public ROVER retrieval limitation is not evidence of non-approval.
July customer delivery and September supplier delivery coverage do not establish actual passenger-service entry, second-unit delivery, current general order acceptance or New-stock availability.

Volgren reveal-day text (23 June) conflicts with Volvo/PTA (25 June). Preserve publication versus event dates and current versus historical battery/body scopes; older rigid Optimum/NCA sources must not override this Optimus/LFP customer build.
